messages.subject: Re: passing variabel from php to script.r and return the result back to php
parts:
You'll need to decide on a framework for issuing ajax calls to your server.  I'm using Dojo but there are others you can choose from.  Do some investigation and reading on these to understand how the are setup.

To do ajax calls in Dojo, it is very easy.  Here is a sample javascript (you'll have to modify it to work in your specific environment for your purposes...)

<script>
function R_function(rData){
        
        require(["dojo/request"], function(request){
        request.post("R/myscript.R", {
          data: {
            sync: true,
            data: rData
          }
        }).then(function(output){
           rReturnObj = JSON.parse(output);
           return(rReturnObj);
        });
      });
    }
</script>

You can then have a similar javascript function for your PHP call:

<script>
function PHP_function(phpData){
        
        require(["dojo/request"], function(request){
        request.post("/php/myscript.php", {
          data: {
            sync: true,
            data: phpData
          }
        }).then(function(output){
           phpReturnObj = JSON.parse(output);
           return(phpReturnObj);
        });
      });
    }
</script>

We assume that both your PHP and R scripts return JSON.  The R script will have something like myData = POST("rData") or if rData is JSON, it would be myData = fromJSON(POST("rData")) somewhere in the first few lines.  Your last line could be something like cat(toJSON(returnData)).  For your PHP script, you'd have something similar (I don't know PHP unfortunately).

Then you can have a javascript that does:

<script>
  ...code that creates rData ..
  rObj = R_script(rData);
  ...more processing creating phpData ...
  phpObj = PHP_script(phpData)
  ... more processing...
</script>

You can attach this script within our HTML page where the processing needs to occur.

The current version of Dojo  supports asynchronous communications so the sync:true would be used to ensure that the first call is completed before the next call is executed.

Frankly speaking, a more efficient way to do this if both R and PHP are on the same server is to simply determine how to call the r script from php or vice versa.  Perhaps system calls together with parameterized shell scripts might be useful.
